subject: Dedicated pool lease window & burst policy — ops/product alignment
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool lease window & burst policy — ops/product alignment

Hi team,

Quick note to align on NovaHealth's upcoming pilot. They signed the SOW that pins a dedicated GPU pool for a 7-day pilot window in September (deal NH-ENTERPRISE-2028-04). Product needs a predictable performance window for load tests and end-to-end validation; sales committed to an explicit reserved lane.

Asks:
- Can infra provision a reserved pool (8x A100-equivalent slots) for a contiguous 7-day lease in the week of Sept 11–17?
- Can we allow a one-time autoscale "burst" beyond the reserved count (up to +50%) for two hours in the middle of that window for validation traffic, with a hard cap?
- Ops: what would be the cost delta and operational risk? Any limits on concurrent KV cache priming or warmup that would affect latency during burst?

I've attached a draft lease plan (draft-lease-plan.xlsx) — it's lightweight, includes a proposed schedule and fallback model. Sales / finance: Karthik / Marissa, please confirm the level of discount/credit we promised so infra can estimate cost exposure.

If we can't support a burst exception, product would rather shorten the window than risk flaky validation. Suggested decision target: next Wed EOD (2028-06-21) so procurement can finalize the schedule.

Thanks — Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool lease window & burst policy — ops/product alignment

Grace —

Thanks for the clear ask and the draft plan. Short answer: technically feasible, but we need to lock a few constraints and mitigation steps before we greenlight the burst exception. Key points: 

1) Reservation schedule: we can reserve 8 slots (A100-equivalent) for Sept 11–17. We'll implement node pinning in the pool to avoid noisy neighbors. Impact: minimal on other tenants if we pre-book capacity now.

2) Burst policy: we can enable a temporary burst up to +50% for a 2h window, but it requires:
   - A pre-warm sequence (KV-cache priming) 30–45 minutes before the burst. If the customer tries to hit the burst cold, they will see higher p99s.
   - Autoscaler guardrails: we can set a hard cap and an emergency fallback to lower-quality model variants (quantized) if nodes aren't available.

3) Cost & ops: rough estimate — incremental cost for 2h burst (cloud hour + premium) is ~USD 2,300 above the reserved-week baseline for 8->12 slots on top of storage egress and warmup execution. That's a live estimate; I'll validate with infra billing and update.

4) Risks: concurrent cache priming can saturate network egress if multiple heavy sequences run; recommend we reserve a 45-minute warmup window where only NovaHealth traffic runs. That reduces risk of cross-tenant interference.

Attached: draft-lease-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet) — I added an ops appendix with warmup steps and rollback plan.

If this is acceptable, I'll add the burst guardrails into the deployment manifest and schedule a rehearsal.

- Dev

[attachment: draft-lease-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool lease window & burst policy — ops/product alignment

Team —

From the sales/finance side: NovaHealth agreed to the reserved-week model in principle. The procurement team pushed back on an unconditional burst because they want predictability on spend. We verbally committed to a one-time validation burst, but procurement requires: 

- A capped dollar exposure (they asked for "no more than $3k incremental"), and
- An explicit rollback clause: if the burst hits more than 80% p99 violation, Redwood will revert to the reserved baseline and issue credits for the validation run.

Proposed compromise: allow the 2h burst with a soft cap of $2,800 and the warmup window Dev recommended. If infra's estimate stays near $2.3k, procurement should accept that as long as we include the rollback SLA in the contract addendum.

Marissa will confirm final negotiation language; she also asked whether we can offer a one-time trial credit if the customer signs an annual commit after pilot. I suggest we hold that conversation until we finalize the cost exposure.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Mills <jared@novahealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool lease window & burst policy — ops/product alignment

Thanks all — summary below for procurement and ops playbook. Looping in Jared so NovaHealth sees the plan.

Decision summary (action items):
- Reserve 8 A100-equivalent slots Sept 11–17 (Dev to provision by 2028-08-21).
- Approve one-time 2h burst up to +50% (i.e., 8 -> 12 slots) with a hard dollar cap of $2,800. Dev to validate exact cost with infra billing and confirm before we sign.
- Warmup: 45-minute KV-cache priming window starting 30 minutes before the burst; NovaHealth to run priming scripts during that time.
- Rollback & SLA: If the burst causes >80% p99 violation or other service degradation, Redwood will terminate the burst and offer a pilot credit (to be quantified by finance).
- Next steps: Dev to update the lease manifest and ops runbook; Marissa to negotiate the addendum language with procurement; Karthik to confirm credit terms. Decision target met: we have a provisional plan; finalize numbers by 2028-06-21.

I've attached the runbook stub (lease-runbook-v1.pdf) with a short checklist for rehearsal and rollback. Please flag anything missing or operationally risky. If all good, I'll send the schedule to NovaHealth procurement and request the official DocuSign addendum.

Thanks — Grace

[attachment: lease-runbook-v1.pdf (document)]
